forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. April 2026 saw GPT-5.5 (OpenAI), Claude Mythos 5 (Anthropic, 10T params), Gemini 3.1 (Google) — all major capability releases but none claimed AGI. Anthropic established AGI think tank March 2026; Amazon committed $25B and Google up to $40B to Anthropic. Capital and capability rising but no credible AGI declaration. Metaculus median AGI ~mid-2030 (after deadline). Resolution requires lab declaration before 1 Jan 2030 — <45 months remaining.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi, expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Three top labs released frontier models in April 2026 (+2pp)
Massive capital flowing to Anthropic and OpenAI (+2pp)
Anthropic's formal AGI societal-impact think tank (+2pp)
Hassabis and Altman publicly maintaining 2027-2030 timeline (+2pp)
factors_down: No credible lab has claimed AGI achievement (-4pp)
Fortune reports OpenAI 'drama' may delay IPO/scaling (-1pp)

Whether scaling returns hold at 10T+ parameter regime
Pace of autonomous R&D / agentic milestones in 2026-27

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3%. Latest Electoral Calculus MRP (April 2026) puts Labour at 17% on 86 seats; Ipsos shows Reform with 6-point lead (Labour and Conservatives tied 19%); YouGov has Labour at 16% in fourth place. Bloomberg notes Labour 'in fourth at start of month-long sprint to UK elections' (local elections 7 May). Bloomberg composite: 17.3% Labour. Next GE still expected by Aug 2029 — 3+ years for recovery, but Labour now consistently fourth or third.

factors_up: 3+ years remain for Labour to recover (+3pp)
Reform support may prove shallow under government scrutiny (+2pp)
FPTP can deliver large seat shifts on small vote-share moves (+1pp)

Timing of next general election (likely 2029 but earlier possible)
Whether Labour replaces leadership before next GE

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. ONS March 2026 CPI at 3.3% (up from 3.0% Feb), driven by transport (+4.7% YoY) and motor fuels reflecting Middle East energy spike. Core CPIH 3.3%. Services inflation 4.3% YoY. Trajectory is wrong direction. With ~8 months of CPI prints remaining before 1 Jan 2027, sub-2.0% would require sharp services disinflation and energy reversal — highly unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: <5% — UK CPI hasn't fallen below 2% since mid-2021; current trend rising
factors_up: BoE could cut rates if growth weakens (+1pp)
Energy prices could revert sharply if Middle East de-escalates (+1pp)
factors_down: March CPI at 3.3% — well above threshold (-3pp)
Only 8 months of prints remain before deadline (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether energy prices reverse in H2 2026
Pace of services-price disinflation
Whether UK enters recession that triggers sharp disinflation

update_triggers.up: Sharp energy-price reversal; recession; CPI prints fall to 2.5% or below
update_triggers.down: CPI rises further above 3.5%; services inflation stickier
